tool.name: ProteinQuantifier
tool.command:
@QUOTE_FOO@ @EXT_FOO@ #import re
## Preprocessing mkdir in && cp '$in' 'in/${gxy_input_basename($in.element_identifier, $in.ext)}' && #if $protein_groups: mkdir protein_groups && cp '$protein_groups' 'protein_groups/${gxy_input_basename($protein_groups.element_identifier, $protein_groups.ext)}' && #end if #if $design: mkdir design && cp '$design' 'design/${gxy_input_basename($design.element_identifier, $design.ext)}' && #end if #if "out_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') mkdir out && #end if #if "peptide_out_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') mkdir peptide_out && #end if #if "mztab_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') mkdir mztab && #end if #if "out_qpx_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') mkdir out_qpx && #end if
## Main program call
set -o pipefail && @EXECUTABLE@ -write_ctd ./ && python3 '$__tool_directory__/fill_ctd.py' '@EXECUTABLE@.ctd' '$args_json' '$hardcoded_json' && @EXECUTABLE@ -ini @EXECUTABLE@.ctd -in 'in/${gxy_input_basename($in.element_identifier, $in.ext)}' #if $protein_groups: -protein_groups 'protein_groups/${gxy_input_basename($protein_groups.element_identifier, $protein_groups.ext)}' #end if #if $design: -design 'design/${gxy_input_basename($design.element_identifier, $design.ext)}' #end if #if "out_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') -out 'out/output.${gxy2omsext("csv")}' #end if #if "peptide_out_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') -peptide_out 'peptide_out/output.${gxy2omsext("csv")}' #end if #if "mztab_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') -mztab 'mztab/output.${gxy2omsext("mztab")}' #end if #if "out_qpx_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') -out_qpx out_qpx/ #end if #if len(str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',')) == 0 | tee '$stdout' #end if
## Postprocessing #if "out_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') && mv 'out/output.${gxy2omsext("csv")}' '$out' #end if #if "peptide_out_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') && mv 'peptide_out/output.${gxy2omsext("csv")}' '$peptide_out' #end if #if "mztab_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') && mv 'mztab/output.${gxy2omsext("mztab")}' '$mztab' #end if #if "ctd_out_FLAG" in $OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS && mv '@EXECUTABLE@.ctd' '$ctd_out' #end if

param.label: Protein inference results for the identification runs that were used to annotate the input
param.help: (e.g. via the ProteinInference tool).. Information about indistinguishable proteins will be used for protein quantification select idxml data sets(s)

param.label: input file containing the experimental design
- top - quantify based on three most abundant peptides (number can be changed in 'top')
param.help: - iBAQ (intensity based absolute quantification), calculate the sum of all peptide peak intensities divided by the number of theoretically observable tryptic peptides (https://rdcu.be/cND1J). Warning: only consensusXML or featureXML input is allowed!

param.label: Distinguish between fraction and charge states in detailed peptide output
param.help: For protein quantification, select one charge per modified peptide globally: maximize the number of (fraction group, label) assays with a positive abundance, then break ties by total abundance; retain that charge's values in every assay.. By default, protein abundances are summed over all charge states. How the retained values of several fractions are combined is governed by 'fractions:aggregate', not by this flag

param.label: Pre-process identifications with greedy resolution of shared peptides based on the protein group probabilities
param.help: (Only works with an idXML file given as protein_groups parameter)

param.label: Output protein abundances with detailed file+channel level headers (similar to detailed peptide output)
param.help: When enabled, protein output will show abundance_filename_channel columns instead of assay columns.. Note that peptide selection and aggregation are then applied per file, not per assay: 'top:N' requires N peptides in that single file (much stricter than the assay-level rule for fractionated data, where all cells of a quantified protein can end up 0), and the cells only decompose the assay-level value for 'top:N' 0 with 'top:aggregate' sum

section.name: top
section.title: Additional options for custom quantification using top N peptides

param.name: N
param.label: Calculate protein abundance from this number of proteotypic peptides (most abundant first; '0' for all)

param.name: aggregate
param.label: Aggregation method used to compute protein abundances from peptide abundances

param.name: include_all
param.label: Include results for proteins with fewer proteotypic peptides than indicated by 'N' (no effect if 'N' is 0 or 1)

section.name: fractions
section.title: Options for combining the fractions of a fraction group

param.name: aggregate
param.label: How the fractions of one fraction group are combined into that group's (fraction group, label) assay values
param.help: - sum - add up every fraction, i.e. treat them as the parts of one separated sample that they are.. - best - keep a single fraction per peptide and fraction group and discard the others. The fraction is chosen ONCE per peptide, ranked by the number of labels in which it has a positive abundance and then by the total of those abundances (an exact tie keeps the lowest fraction number), and ALL of its labels are then taken from it. The choice is deliberately not made per label: taking one channel from one fraction and another channel from a different fraction would mix physical aliquots and destroy the reporter-ion ratios that isobaric quantification consists of.. Only the assay values are affected. Per-(file, channel) quantities are per fraction by definition and always report every file

section.name: consensus
section.title: Additional options for consensus maps (and identification results comprising multiple runs)

param.name: normalize
param.label: Scale peptide abundances so that the median of each (fraction group, label) assay matches the overall median
param.help: Abundances of zero count as 'not detected' and are left out of the medians; an assay without any positive abundance takes no part in the normalization

param.name: fix_peptides
param.label: Use the same peptides for protein quantification across all (fraction group, label) assays
param.help: With 'N 0',all peptides that occur in every assay are considered.. Otherwise ('N'), the N peptides that occur in the most assays (independently of each other) are selected,. breaking ties by total abundance (there is no guarantee that the best co-ocurring peptides are chosen!).. A peptide counts as occurring in an assay only where its abundance is positive: an abundance stored as zero means 'not detected' (e.g. an isobaric reporter below 'min_reporter_intensity'), not a measurement of absence

param.name: separator
param.label: Character(s) used to separate fields; by default, the 'tab' character is used

param.name: quoting
param.label: Method for quoting of strings: 'none' for no quoting, 'double' for quoting with doubling of embedded quotes
param.help: 'escape' for quoting with backslash-escaping of embedded quotes

param.name: replacement
param.label: If 'quoting' is 'none', used to replace occurrences of the separator in strings before writing
Enables the test mode (needed for internal use only)

param.name: OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS
param.label: Optional outputs
param.option: out_qpx (Output directory for QPX Parquet files (quantms.feature.parquet, quantms.psm.parquet, quantms.pg.parquet))

data.name: out
data.label: ${tool.name} on ${on_string}: out
data.filter: OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS is not None and "out_FLAG" in OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS

data.name: peptide_out
data.label: ${tool.name} on ${on_string}: peptide_out
data.filter: OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS is not None and "peptide_out_FLAG" in OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS

data.name: mztab
data.label: ${tool.name} on ${on_string}: mztab
data.filter: OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS is not None and "mztab_FLAG" in OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS

collection.name: out_qpx
collection.label: ${tool.name} on ${on_string}: out_qpx
collection.filter: OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS is not None and "out_qpx_FLAG" in OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS

data.name: ctd_out
data.label: ${tool.name} on ${on_string}: ctd
data.filter: OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS is not None and "ctd_out_FLAG" in OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS

tool.help:
Compute peptide and protein abundances
For more information, visit https://www.openms.de/doxygen/release/3.6.0/html/TOPP_ProteinQuantifier.html
